# Skills matrix — what changes between rungs

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-skills-matrix.js — do not edit by hand. -->
<!-- Run `npm run build-skills-matrix` after changing a ladder or a role file. -->

Crosses the ladders in [Career Paths & Skills Progression](SKILLS_PROGRESSION.md) with the **Technology Proficiency Levels** of the roles on each rung. 63 transitions across 32 domains. Generated 2026-08.

## How to read it, and what it is not

**Deepens** is a technology both rungs expect, at a higher level on the upper rung. **Adds** is one the upper rung expects and the lower one does not name at all. Where a rung holds several roles, the highest tier among them is used, so the row describes the rung rather than whichever role was listed first.

**This is not a training plan and not an assessment.** It says what the role definitions differ on, which is a starting point for a progression conversation — not a judgement about a person, and not a course list. Turning it into either is work for whoever owns learning and development.

It is also only as complete as the vocabulary in `data/technologies.json`. A technology nobody listed is a technology this matrix cannot see. 12 of the 63 transitions show no change at all, which usually means the two role definitions describe the same technologies and differ on scope and autonomy instead — those differences are in the role files, not here.
